title: Prayer in the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Prayer in the church is the shared dependence of God’s people on the Father through Christ by the Holy Spirit. The church prays in worship, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, need, mission, and spiritual battle.
summary: Prayer in the church is the shared dependence of God’s people on the Father through Christ by the Holy Spirit. The church prays in worship, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, need, mission, and spiritual battle.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives His people access to the Father and teaches them to pray with trust. The church prays in His name, depending on His mediation and seeking His will.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The early church devoted itself to prayer. Prayer was not an accessory to ministry, but a central expression of dependence on God.

The church prays because Christ has opened access to the Father. Believers draw near to the throne of grace through the great High Priest who sympathizes with weakness.

Church prayer includes many burdens: worship, confession, thanksgiving, intercession, healing, mission, leaders, enemies, the suffering, the lost, and the spread of the Gospel.

Prayer also strengthens unity and courage. When the church prayed in Acts, believers were filled with boldness to speak the Word. Prayer keeps the church dependent rather than self-reliant.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
A church may have activity, programs, and plans while quietly losing dependence on God. Prayerlessness reveals misplaced confidence.

This doctrine reminds believers that the church is not sustained by human strength. The weak, sick, grieving, tempted, and burdened need a praying people who bring needs before the Lord together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in the prayer life of the church. Pray for leaders, the weak, the lost, the suffering, and the advance of the Gospel. Do not treat prayer as a last resort. Come boldly through Christ and help your church remain dependent on God.
